title: Relative bicentralizers and core commutants
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: Relative bicentralizers of inclusions with expectation and the commutant of the bottom algebra in the continuous core. The relative bicentralizer, its description in the Ocneanu ultrapower, its expectation as a limit of averages over almost centralizing unitaries; Connes' transition isomorphisms, the relative bicentralizer flow of Ando, Haagerup, Houdayer and Marrakchi, and the state-independent algebra generated by the bottom algebra and the relative bicentralizer; Marrakchi's binormal identity, proved through a tracial corner of the continuous core; approximate eigenoperators and Marrakchi's spectral shift maps; and OpenAI's proof (2026) that the two relative products of the bottom algebra and the relative bicentralizer differ exactly by the flow, through an iterated completely positive kernel, an estimate uniform in total modular energy and repeated random tensor tests. Consequences: the core fixed point theorem and a criterion for subalgebras with the same relative commutant in the core. Finally, finite-dimensional subfactors, state changes and the lifting of matrix units from the asymptotic centralizer, and the main theorem of OpenAI for bottom factors of type III_1: an approximately finite-dimensional subalgebra, invariant under the modular group of a suitable state, with the same relative commutant in the continuous core, built by an inductive construction after Ando, Haagerup, Houdayer and Marrakchi; and, for a single factor of type III_1, Haagerup's theorem that the faithful normal states with irreducible centralizer are norm dense. The last lesson treats semifinite bottom factors: Popa's hyperfinite subfactor with the same relative commutant for factors of type II_1, a matrix amplification with an almost periodic state for type II_infinity, and the resulting theorem for every semifinite bottom factor.
prerequisites: bicentralizers-of-type-iii1-factors (all lessons; in particular the asymptotic centralizer, the bicentralizer flow, modular averaging Lemmas 1.1-1.2, strongly invariant states Lemma 3.3, and Theorem 6.1 that the bicentralizer of a type III_1 factor is trivial)

open_obligations: OpenAI, Expected amenable subalgebras preserving core commutants (23 Sep 2026), Theorem 1.1, for bottom factors of type III_lambda (0 <= lambda < 1) and for bottom algebras with nontrivial centre. The course proves the theorem when N is a factor of type III_1 (an-injective-subalgebra-with-the-same-core-commutant, Theorem 5.2) or a semifinite factor (semifinite-bottom-factors, Theorem 4.1), with separable preduals. Missing: factors of type III_lambda, 0 <= lambda < 1 (OpenAI uses arXiv 2308.15163, Proposition 4.11: discrete decomposition and the weak Dixmier property; a direct route would use periodic or almost periodic states, cf. type-iii-factors almost-periodic-weights lesson Theorem 5.5 and AHHM Theorem 5.5, with the centralizer criterion semifinite-bottom-factors Lemma 1.1), and general N with arbitrary centre (disintegration over the centre: Ichihara-Kawakami 2007, Propositions 2.1-2.2 and Theorem 2.3; arXiv 2308.15163, Propositions 4.7 and 4.12; OpenAI's averaging into the central commutant; arXiv 2308.15163, Theorem D). Owner: Claude. Not written.

Not written.

OpenAI Section 3 (alternative proof of the separable instance of the Houdayer-Marrakchi theorem that type III_1 factors have trivial bicentralizer, via the two multiplication maps and a spectral lattice argument; uses Marrakchi arXiv 1811.10253, Theorem D, and Houdayer-Isono arXiv 1503.01388, Proposition 3.4 and Theorem 3.5). Marrakchi arXiv 2606.23636: Lemma 2.2(2)-(3); Theorem A (maximal abelian subalgebras A in N with A' cap M = A v (N' cap M)); Theorem B (an AFD P in N with expectation and P' cap M = N' cap M) for bottom algebras other than factors of type III_1; Theorem C in full (fixed points and eigenvectors of the relative bicentralizer flow); and arXiv 2308.15163, Theorem 2.9 (ultrapower implementation of binormal states for all types). The course proves the sequence form of binormal states needed here (binormal lesson, Theorems 2.4 and 4.2), and its Theorem 5.2 gives P' cap M = N' cap M for factors N of type III_1; the ergodicity part of Theorem C follows from that with AHHM Theorem C, direction (ii) => (i), which is not written in the programme. The reverse inclusion N' cap c(M) subset (B rtimes R)^{gamma^c} of the core fixed point theorem (OpenAI Proposition 7.2 as an equality) and the identification of B rtimes R with the relative bicentralizer of N in c(M) (arXiv 2308.15163, Propositions 7.2, 8.1, 8.4).
